newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures settle lower with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures settle lower with cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Tuesday in tandem in line with physical prices due to outlook of mild weather in the much of the western U.S.
"We saw the numbers traded off with cash today," said one Houston trader.

The complex was also pressured by weaker natural gas prices. December natgas prices delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub ended the day at $2.32-$2.37 per million British thermal units, down two to three cents from Monday.
High prices for next-day peak power from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) failed to support daily power prices in the Northwest.
The federal marketing agency increased offers of daily, peak electricity by $1.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) to $25.25.
December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished at $23.05, down 40 cents after hitting a low of $22.60.
January COB settled down 26 cents at $20.44 after bouncing between $20.15-$20.50. Deferred COB months ended down 15 to 24 cents.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures finished down 35 cents at $21.05 after reaching as low as $20.75.
Januaray PV settled down three cents at $19.30, almost erasing at 43 cent loss. Outer PV contracts ended mixed.
Most brokers and traders expected the complex to continue its recent losses Wednesday.
"I don't see any fundamentals to bring it back up," said another Houston trader.
According to the latest forecasts, much of the West was expected to experience normal to above-normal temperatures for the rest of the week.
NYMEX estimated 119 COB and 96 PV contracts changed hands.
